title: Formula Sheet & Sign Rules Cheat Sheet
objectives: Quickly review all integer sign rules, absolute values, and comparison laws on a single sheet

blocks.heading: Integer Hierarchy & Sets
blocks.content:
• **Natural Numbers (N):** $\{1, 2, 3, 4, \dots\}$
• **Whole Numbers (W):** $\{0, 1, 2, 3, 4, \dots\} = \mathbb{N} \cup \{0\}$
• **Integers (Z):** $\{\dots, -3, -2, -1, 0, 1, 2, 3, \dots\}$
• Note: Zero ($0$) is neither positive nor negative.

blocks.heading: The Master Sign Matrix
blocks.content:
| Operation | Rule | Example |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| $(+) + (+)$ | Add magnitudes, keep $+$ | $4 + 7 = +11$ |
| $(-) + (-)$ | Add magnitudes, keep $-$ | $(-3) + (-5) = -8$ |
| $(+) + (-)$ | Subtract magnitudes, take larger sign | $8 + (-5) = +3$ |
| $(-) + (+)$ | Subtract magnitudes, take larger sign | $(-9) + 4 = -5$ |
| $-(-x)$ | Double negative becomes positive | $10 - (-3) = 10 + 3 = 13$ |
| $+(-x)$ | Plus followed by minus is negative | $12 + (-4) = 12 - 4 = 8$ |

blocks.heading: Top 3 Board & Exam Traps
blocks.content:
⚠️ **Trap 1: Confusing Addition with Multiplication.** In addition, $(-2) + (-3) = -5$ (debt increases). Do NOT say 'minus into minus is plus' here!

⚠️ **Trap 2: Ordering Negative Numbers.** With negative numbers, larger absolute value means smaller number! E.g., $-100 < -1$, not $>$.

⚠️ **Trap 3: Absolute Value.** $|x| \ge 0$ always. $|-7| = 7$ and $|+7| = 7$.

workedExamples.prompt: Quick Revision Check: Which is greater: -18 or -11?
steps: Step 1: On the number line, -11 is to the right of -18.

practice.prompt: What is the additive inverse of -47?
hints: The additive inverse of a number x is -x such that x + (-x) = 0.
practice.feedback: The additive inverse of -47 is +47, because (-47) + 47 = 0.

takeaways: Keep this formula card handy for mental sign checks.
Never apply multiplication sign rules to addition.
